statements.impact_statement: crypto/x509's chain verification with untrusted intermediates runs when a Go program verifies a peer's certificate as a TLS client. Caddy in this image never does: deploy/Caddyfile sets auto_https off (no ACME), serves its own certificate from /data/certs, and proxies to plain-http upstreams on localhost (reverse_proxy to the Flask backend and the central server); it verifies no certificate. Fixed upstream in Go 1.26.10 / 1.27.3; the Caddy build moved to golang:1.27.3-alpine on 2026-11-05 (the release after 4.0.1, docs/security/urgent-updates.md), so the flawed stdlib is no longer in the image and this statement covers the releases built with 1.27.2.

This is pip's vendored urllib3 (pip/_vendor/urllib3, pip 26.2.1's vendor.txt), imported by pip alone; pip runs only during the image build. The application and its packages import the urllib3 that backend/requirements.lock installs (2.8.0, which has the fix), never pip's copy. The HTTPS-proxy TLS override needs an HTTPS proxy configured for a running urllib3, which the image has nowhere.

pip's vendored urllib3 (pip/_vendor), imported by pip alone, which runs only while the image is built; the application's urllib3 is 2.8.0 from backend/requirements.lock, where the chunked-encoding fix is in.

pip's vendored msgpack (pip/_vendor/msgpack), which pip uses for its HTTP cache during an install; pip runs only while the image is built. Nothing in backend/requirements.lock depends on msgpack and the application never imports it, so no Unpacker is ever reused on untrusted data at runtime.

setuptools' PackageIndex.download is the easy_install-era downloader, run only by setup.py-driven installs that fetch distributions by URL. No setuptools module is importable by either interpreter in the image (the application's /opt/app-root/bin/python and the system python3.14 both answer ModuleNotFoundError, checked in the built image): the scanner's hit is package metadata of the base image's build tooling, not an installed package, and the application installs nothing at runtime.

brotlicffi is locked with the marker platform_python_implementation == 'PyPy' (Flask-Compress's PyPy dependency); Jacarium runs on CPython in the container and in the desktop app, where the marker is false and pip never installs it - CPython uses brotli 1.2.1, which carries the fix. Checked: not importable in the built image, absent from the desktop venv. OSV-Scanner lists it because it reads the lock line by line without evaluating environment markers.

The remaining 3.1.5 and 5.1.9 copies (glob 7 under @electron/asar, dir-compare, filelist - all in electron-builder's dev tree, not shipped) have no first- or second-phase preprocessing of glob parts and no optimizationLevel option, which is where the advisory's amplification lives (the optimizationLevel passes came with minimatch 7.1; the fix is in 11.0.1). The copies that had that code, 9.0.9 and 10.2.6, are overridden to 11.0.3. The remaining copies also only ever see the project's own file patterns, never a user's or the network's.

The base image's npm (nodejs / npm RPMs) and its bundled brace-expansion are removed from the image in deploy/Containerfile; /usr/lib/node_modules no longer exists. The application's Node is the Node 24 binary from the UI build stage, and its own dependencies come from package-lock.json, which the lock-file scan covers.

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable code is the sqlite3 command-line shell's .recover command (shell.c), and the shell is not in the image: only sqlite-libs (libsqlite3.so.0) is installed, the `sqlite` RPM that ships /usr/bin/sqlite3 is not, and `command -v sqlite3` finds nothing - deploy/Containerfile's runtime stage checks both at build time. The backend uses the library alone (Python's sqlite3 module for its databases), which has no .recover and runs no dot-commands. Node's bundled SQLite (node:sqlite, the nodejs.org binary) is library code too, with no .recover in its API. Nothing in the image can run the shell's recovery output.

decode_sequence_of() is libkrb5's ASN.1 decoder; the denial of service is a KDC decoding a hostile AS-REQ / TGS-REQ, and no KDC is in the image. On the client side nothing here decodes Kerberos messages either: Jacarium does no Kerberos or GSSAPI authentication (the backend's HTTP is Python's, never libcurl; no --negotiate, no SASL GSSAPI), there is no credential cache, keytab or kinit, and the ssh client - whose Red Hat default offers GSSAPIAuthentication - stops at acquiring credentials, before any exchange with a KDC. Checked in the 4.4.3 image: only krb5-libs is installed (no krb5-server, krb5-workstation or libkadm5: no kadmind, krb5kdc, kadmin or kinit binary, no libkadm5 / libkdb5).

get_pac_princ_with_realm() is in the KDC (krb5kdc) and is reached by an S4U2Proxy request from a cross-realm KDC; no KDC is in the image. Checked in the 4.4.3 image: only krb5-libs is installed (no krb5-server, krb5-workstation or libkadm5: no kadmind, krb5kdc, kadmin or kinit binary, no libkadm5 / libkdb5).

The read overrun is in the ASN.1 decoder as a KDC runs it on an unauthenticated request; no KDC is in the image, and nothing here decodes Kerberos messages on the client side either. Jacarium does no Kerberos or GSSAPI authentication and accepts none: there is no credential cache, keytab or kinit, no sshd or other GSS-API acceptor, and the ssh client's GSSAPIAuthentication default stops at acquiring credentials.
